blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Presenting to a board is not the same activity as presenting to a team, however similar the slides may look. A board audience has, collectively, hundreds of years of business experience, has seen dozens of similar stories before, and has developed a near-infallible sense for when a presenter is overclaiming, hiding something, or simply out of their depth.

The mistake many senior presenters make is to treat board time as if it were classroom time — walking the audience through what they already know, before arriving at the actual question. Board members almost always want to start where the presenter wants to finish. State the recommendation in the first two minutes. Explain the reasoning, compactly, across the next eight. Leave generous room for questions, which is where the real conversation happens.

Rarely is a board won over by enthusiasm; still more rarely by defensiveness. What tends to earn their trust is the presenter's willingness to name the uncomfortable facts themselves, before any board member can do so. A presenter who opens with "There are three things that might worry you, and I would like to address each directly" instantly changes the dynamic in the room.

items.q: According to the text, why is a board audience difficult to present to?
options: They insist on being walked through the basics
They lack the time to ask questions
They rarely read the slides in advance
They have vast experience and detect overclaiming instantly
items.why: "hundreds of years of business experience… a near-infallible sense for when a presenter is overclaiming."

items.q: How does the text say a presenter should structure board time?
options: Cover everything the board already knows, then stop
Build context first, then reveal the recommendation at the end
Spend most of the time defending the numbers
Recommendation first, compact reasoning, then generous room for questions
items.why: "State the recommendation in the first two minutes… across the next eight… Leave generous room for questions."

items.q: The phrase "Board members almost always want to start where the presenter wants to finish" suggests that…
options: boards prefer presentations to run long
boards want the conclusion up front, not at the end
presenters and boards rarely agree on anything
presenters should never state a recommendation
items.why: Inferência: o 'finish' do apresentador é a recomendação; o conselho quer começar por ela.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Naming your own weak points can build credibility
Boards can sense when a presenter is out of their depth
Questions are where the real conversation happens
A confident, enthusiastic pitch is what wins a board over
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que raramente a plateia é conquistada por entusiasmo — 'Rarely is a board won over by enthusiasm'.

items.q: Why does opening with "There are three things that might worry you" change the dynamic?
options: It hands control of the agenda to the board
It signals the presenter is short of time
It shows the presenter is honest and ahead of the objections
It avoids discussing the recommendation altogether
items.why: Inferência: ao nomear os fatos incômodos primeiro, o apresentador demonstra franqueza e antecipa as críticas.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James abrindo sua apresentação de alocação de capital ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning. Before I take you through the analysis, let me state the recommendation plainly: we should commit the full one hundred and twenty million to the Rotterdam expansion, and defer the two smaller bolt-ons entirely.

Now, I know how this room works, so I would rather name the three things that might worry you than wait for you to raise them. First, the payback period is eleven months longer than the board's usual threshold; I will not pretend otherwise. Second, roughly a third of the projected upside depends on a freight cost assumption that could move against us. And third, we would concentrate capital in a single site rather than spread the risk.

I have looked hard at each of those, and I still recommend we proceed — but I want you to challenge me on all three, because that is where this decision will actually be made.

So rather than walk you through forty slides, I have kept the reasoning to eight minutes and left the rest of the hour for your questions. Shall I begin with the freight assumption, since I suspect that is the one that concerns you most?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James do in the very first part of his presentation?
options: He reviews the last quarter's results
He asks the board what they already know
He states the recommendation plainly
He apologises for the length of the deck
items.why: "let me state the recommendation plainly: we should commit the full one hundred and twenty million."

items.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three concerns James names himself?
options: Part of the upside rests on a freight cost assumption
Capital would be concentrated in a single site
The project team lacks relevant experience
The payback period exceeds the usual threshold
items.why: Ele cita payback longo, premissa de frete e concentração em um só site — nunca falta de experiência da equipe.

items.q: Why does James raise the three concerns before the board can?
options: Because the board asked him to list the risks
To recommend that the board reject the project
To fill time before the questions begin
To front-run the objections and protect his credibility
items.why: Inferência: antecipar os pontos fracos (front-run) demonstra franqueza e mantém a credibilidade.

items.q: What does James's closing question about the freight assumption reveal?
options: He wants to avoid discussing that point
He has run out of prepared material
He has read the room and expects it to be their main worry
He is unsure which figure is correct
items.why: Inferência: 'since I suspect that is the one that concerns you most' mostra que ele leu a plateia e escolheu enfrentar o ponto mais sensível primeiro.

items.q: How would you best describe James's approach in this opening?
options: Cautious, deferring the recommendation to the end
Direct and candid, inviting challenge
Enthusiastic but light on detail
Defensive and evasive about the risks
items.why: Inferência: ele nomeia os riscos, pede que o desafiem e vai direto ao ponto — franqueza, não defensividade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The deck was polished, but he kept overclaiming until the CFO stopped believing the numbers." To overclaim is to…
options: repeat a point for emphasis
assert more than the evidence supports
understate the results deliberately
request additional funding
items.why: Overclaim = afirmar em excesso, prometer mais do que a evidência sustenta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She lost the room the moment she slipped into ___, defending every figure instead of engaging with the challenge."
options: defensiveness
rigour
recommendation
credibility
items.why: Defensiveness = defensividade: reagir defendendo-se em vez de dialogar.

items.q: "By naming the risks first, he chose to own the uncomfortable facts before anyone else could." This means he…
options: concealed the weak points of the case
took responsibility for the difficult truths himself
delegated the bad news to a colleague
disputed that the risks were real
items.why: To own the uncomfortable facts = assumir os fatos incômodos, trazê-los você mesmo antes que outro o faça.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The whole case rested on his ___ — once the board doubted his honesty, the numbers no longer mattered."
options: credibility
line of questioning
skim audience
boardroom
items.why: Credibility = credibilidade: sem ela, os dados perdem força.

items.q: "He answered with rigour, tracing each figure back to its source." Rigour here means…
options: excessive length and detail
careful, disciplined thoroughness
a rigid, inflexible attitude
emotional intensity
items.why: Rigour = rigor: precisão e disciplina no raciocínio — não rigidez.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em apresentações ao conselho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Good presenters front-run the hard questions." To front-run a question means to…
options: answer it as briefly as possible
pass it to someone else
raise and address it before the audience does
avoid it until the very end
items.why: Front-run = antecipar: trazer a questão difícil você mesmo, antes que a plateia a levante.

items.q: "The chair asked him to get to the point before he had finished the context." This means to…
options: hand over to the next speaker
reach the main message quickly
repeat the recommendation
add more background detail
items.why: Get to the point = ir direto ao ponto, chegar logo à mensagem central.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the freight assumption." They…
options: challenged or resisted it
ignored it entirely
endorsed it immediately
asked for it in writing
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the capital request." To sign off on means to…
options: postpone indefinitely
announce to the market
formally approve
comment informally
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "None of that polish will move the needle if the board doubts his honesty." This means it will…
options: cost more than expected
not make a meaningful difference
provoke open resistance
take too long to prepare
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
